headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors if transformers processes python-cheatsheet outputs in a shared workspace; prompt injection is low because the cheat sheet is documentation-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is documentation-only with no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly inject into agent_b. agent_b can read files and parse stdin/stdout, so only an unusual manual copy-paste or external bridge could create a prompt-injection path. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a text into agent_b prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or message queue is introduced between the agents, agent_b may parse attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep the agents separated with no copy-paste bridge.
Disable any shared inbox, queue, or shared prompt file.
Review agent_b inputs for instruction-like text before execution.
Use a fixed template that strips markdown and directives.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no read/write surfaces, but agent_b can read files and has broad network egress, so any shared workspace or copied content could leak into external calls. Because the pair lacks an explicit shared filesystem in the profiles, this is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, agent_b can read content originating from agent_a's outputs.
IF agent_b sends its context or file contents to external services, copied material may leave the environment.
mitigations: Do not place both agents on the same workspace.
Run agent_b with network egress disabled for sensitive runs.
Copy only minimal excerpts into agent_b.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write files, modify git, or spawn processes, while agent_b can write files and modify local state through shell and subprocesses. That means there is little direct write-write conflict between them; the main risk is only if an external orchestrator gives them the same mutable target, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator maps both agents to the same writable directory, agent_b may overwrite artifacts associated with agent_a.
IF agent_a is later given write access, concurrent edits could conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared git branches for the pair.
Serialize writes through one operator step.
Check for file collisions before running agent_b.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a content-writing reference source and agent_b is a document-processing system with stdin/stdout and file inputs, so agent_b may treat agent_a's text as authoritative unless the operator inserts verification. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default document pipelines, but the blast radius is limited to downstream work products rather than irreversible harm.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output as source text without a verification step, errors can cascade into generated documents.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-apply extracted facts, incorrect content may propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require a human verification step between agents.
Ask agent_b to cite source passages explicitly.
Use a checksum or diff against the original text.
Limit agent_b to summarization, not action-taking.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated secret handling is documented for either agent. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b's listed classes are generic multimodal content, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the workflow, reassess compliance.
IF either agent is later granted residency-constrained data, compliance risk may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Review retention settings for any downstream storage.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
